A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same G-reasoner work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including rendered figures, tables, and equations, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original QA and retrieval experiments on six benchmarks, component ablations, graph-generalization tests, efficiency measurements, and appendix case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds multi-step RAG comparisons, a full-development-set MuSiQue evaluation, and scored reasoning-path examples.

M1.justification: The approach in Section 4 is unchanged: QuadGraph, the 34M-parameter GNN, training objectives, distributed message-passing, and top-k retrieval and LLM prompting are retained. The new gradient-scored paths are presented as post-hoc case analysis, without a reported change to training or answer inference.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training sources and six evaluation benchmarks. MuSiQue-Full expands the development-set sample and supporting/distractor corpus within the existing multi-hop QA coverage; it does not introduce a new domain, task, or document type.

E2.justification: v2 Table 10 adds IRCoT, R1-searcher, and Search-R1 comparisons on all three multi-hop QA benchmarks, substantially extending comparison with iterative retrieval and reasoning systems. Tables 2 and 3 also newly evaluate GFM-RAG on G-bench Novel and Medical, where v1 reported dashes. Existing comparators are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix D.2 adds evaluation on 2,417 MuSiQue development questions and 21,100 documents, alongside the retained 1,000-question, 6,119-document experiment. Table 10 adds per-sample timing to the multi-step RAG comparison. The original experiments' metrics and training configurations remain unchanged; supporting/distractor-corpus descriptions mainly clarify existing settings.

E4.justification: v2 adds a larger-corpus robustness check in Appendix D.2 and two gradient-scored reasoning-path case studies in D.5 and Table 16. The component ablations, cross-graph tests, scaling analysis, reasoning-explanation evaluation, and earlier case studies are retained, with some renumbering.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the empirical comparisons. v2 continues the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 substantially expands the reported comparative evidence while retaining existing numerical entries. Table 10 adds multi-step RAG scores and latencies; Table 12 reports MuSiQue-Full results, including G-reasoner's 33.64 EM and 47.89 F1 under the added setting. Tables 2 and 3 fill GFM-RAG's Novel/Medical accuracy entries with 58.6/72.2 and recall entries with 75.9/82.2. Notably, Table 10 reports Search-R1 above G-reasoner on MuSiQue F1, 53.2 versus 52.5.

T1.justification: Appendix D.5 adds Equation 13 defining gradient-based triple importance, together with a gradient-product and chain-rule explanation for ranking reasoning paths. The original graph definitions, training equations, and GPU-scaling formula remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: unified four-layer graph representation, joint topology-and-text reasoning with a 34M-parameter GFM, scalable execution, and strong performance and generalization across six benchmarks. The added scalability wording emphasizes a capability already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of larger-corpus robustness and gradient-ranked reasoning paths, and suggests preliminary retrieval filtering for larger corpora. New Appendix F explicitly identifies text-only graphs, separate GFM/LLM modules, and QA-focused evaluation as limitations. The new interpretation of consistent superiority over multi-step RAG requires qualification by the MuSiQue F1 exception in Table 10.

D1.justification: Appendix C.1 newly details graph-construction steps for HippoRAG, LightRAG, and Youtu-GraphRAG, while B and C clarify supporting/distractor passage pooling. A new footnote discloses a GFM-RAG recall-calculation bug fix and re-evaluation. The reproducibility statement promises code and pretrained weights upon acceptance, but the PDFs do not establish their actual release; existing hardware and hyperparameter disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for IRCoT, R1-searcher, Search-R1, and Zhao et al.'s inductive node-classification work. Appendix A.2 adds a distinction between GFMs designed for node classification/link prediction and GraphRAG. The broader research positioning remains intact; expanded Youtu-GraphRAG and SubgraphRAG descriptions in the main text already appeared in v1's appendix.

P1.justification: The main section order and most existing prose are retained. v2 makes localized language edits, expands graph-construction explanations, inserts two experimental appendix subsections and a limitations section, and adds acknowledgments, ethics, reproducibility, and LLM-use statements. Existing appendix analyses are renumbered rather than replaced.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 10–12 and 16; v1's appendix Tables 10–12 become Tables 13–15. Existing tables and figures are reflowed and relocated, including separating the main QA and retrieval tables across pages and placing the prompt with Appendix E. The seven existing figures and overall visual style are retained.

improvement.justification: The added multi-step RAG comparisons and full MuSiQue evaluation strengthen assessment of the existing efficiency and generalization claims. Expanded construction details, path examples, and explicit limitations also improve transparency. These gains are tempered by limited documentation of the new comparator/timing settings and an overbroad superiority statement contradicted by Search-R1's 53.2 versus G-reasoner's 52.5 MuSiQue F1. The evidence supports a modest net improvement.
